bullets.title: AI CapEx cycle re-engages as META raises $95B, AVGO backstops $63B Anthropic deal
bullets.body: The week's defining macro theme was AI infrastructure financing: META announced a $95B+ equity raise (40M shares at $625 + $60B ATM starting Q1'27), with NVDA, AMD, and AVGO each buying ~$5B. Broadcom separately arranged a $63B debt financing SPV for Anthropic's chip purchases, providing residual value guarantees. These moves collectively cleared the 'equity overhang' narrative that had pressured AI trade for weeks, with GS noting hedge fund net AI exposure had fallen to the 17th percentile—historically a setup for sharp reversals.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler earnings: MSFT Azure +48% beat, GOOGL Search miss reignites AI monetization concerns
bullets.body: MSFT delivered the cleanest print: Azure +48% y/y with F2Q guide of 49-50%, operating margins ~50%, and FCF positive despite $25B bond issuance (first IG deal since 2017). GOOGL was the bear story—Search only +12% vs. 14-15% expected, with AI Mode queries pressuring monetization; GCP grew +103% but lower-margin TPU sales clouded margins. AMZN AWS grew +39% (missed elevated ~43% buyside expectations) but guided 40%+ in both 2027 and 2028, with backlog up $82B q/q to $578B. Hyperscaler capex guidance: AMZN ~$220B '26 / meaningfully more '27; GOOGL $195-205B; MSFT lowered to ~$170B on third-party delays.

bullets.title: INTC worst day since 1974 on PC collapse; semis down 8% Friday, SOX hits 200-day MA for first time since mid-2025
bullets.body: Intel's 4Q guide of $15-16B revenue (vs. $17B consensus) and EPS of $0.25 (vs. $0.45 consensus) triggered a -25% single-session collapse on PC market deterioration, Israel Fab 28 outage (-$300M), and DRAM cost-driven demand destruction. CY26 PC TAM cut to -12% with 2027 expected -10%. Semis closed down ~8% Friday—the 3rd-largest single-day underperformance in 15+ years—with SOXX below its 200-day MA for first time since May 2025 and five consecutive weeks of net Tech selling. Multiple analysts flagged this as a late-cycle signal, with back-end constraints from TXN, PI, and NXPI alongside customer pushouts reinforcing the thesis.

bullets.title: NDX worst month since AI cycle began; equal-weight SPX outperformed cap-weight by ~590bp in October
bullets.body: Nasdaq fell ~5.3% in October (worst since March 2025), SOX -15.4%, while Russell 2000 gained +0.54% and the Dow +1.70%. Equal-weight S&P outperformed cap-weight by ~590bp with 60% of constituents above 50-day MAs vs. 21% in late September. Nine of 11 S&P sectors logged weekly gains in the final week; Healthcare, Materials, Utilities led while Tech and Communications lagged. NYSE new lows beat new highs for 43 straight days. S&P 500 ended October down ~0.93%, now ~3% below ATH of 7,844 with key support at 7,500 (Sept low).

bullets.title: Fed holds, December hike priced at 73-85%; Chair Warsh signals neutral rate likely higher
bullets.body: FOMC held rates at 3.75-4.0% with a 10-2 vote (Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike). Markets are pricing ~73-85% probability of a December 25bp hike, with March as a follow-on. Chair Warsh's press conference was viewed as having a shorter shelf-life than prior chairs as he speaks more for himself. Piper Sandler and JPM both expect a December hike bringing rates to 4.25-4.5%. 22V Research flagged Fed signaling rates need to go 'materially higher.' Q3 GDP printed +3.4% (above 3.2% consensus), driven by 4.9% private final domestic demand growth. Core PCE at 0.32% m/m with 52% of categories rising above 3% y/y.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning at multi-year lows; largest sustained de-grossing in 15+ years creates snapback risk
bullets.body: GS Prime reported global hedge fund net returns down ~4% on a rolling 20-day basis, with TMT-focused funds down 11.9% MTD and systematic L/S down 3.5-3.7% MTD (their first negative month of 2026). Overall gross leverage declined more than in late July/August, now near 2018 extremes. Cumulative de-grossing exceeded 6% of book. US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile. However, prior -3 sigma events in 20-day L/S spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases. Post-midterm seasonality (S&P 500 positive 19/19 times since 1950, average +15%) creates a constructive seasonal backdrop.

bullets.title: AI financing stress: Anthropic IPO filed at ~$1.5T valuation; CoreWeave bonds at 76bp wide vs CDX.IG
bullets.body: Anthropic filed its S-1 with H1'26 revenue of $16.3B (1,400% y/y), adjusted operating margin of +19% in Q2 vs. -129% a year prior, and 11,900+ customers with $100K+ annual spend. Future compute commitments total $657B+ from AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, AVGO, AMD, SpaceX, and others. Barclays' AI-related CDS cohort traded at 76bp wide vs CDX.IG, up from 10bp six months ago. 22V noted Anthropic needs ~$200B+ ARR by 2027 exit to cover compute commitments. Anthropic IPO estimated ~Nov 20 and is viewed as 'the last major AI catalyst through year-end.'

bullets.title: Systematic selling dominated week: $165-220B risk-control unwind, ETFs at 31% of tape
bullets.body: UBS estimated $165-220B in systematic risk-control selling triggered by the vol spike, with $55-70B on Oct 30 alone and $110-150B following Monday. Levered ETFs were positioned to sell $35B concentrated in semis ($16.8B) and QQQ ($10.1B). ETFs hit 31% of tape—the highest full-session level since June—suggesting systematic/top-down selling rather than fundamental liquidation. Pension month-end rebalancing partially offset with an estimated $46B in global equity buying. CTA triggers crossed multiple thresholds; next major triggers were far away at -3% to -8% from entry.

bullets.title: US economy running above speed limit: 3Q GDP +3.4%, private demand +4.9%, core PCE sticky
bullets.body: Q3 real GDP printed +3.4% q/q saar (above 3.2% consensus) with domestic demand at +4.9%—the strongest since 2021Q2 ex-COVID. Tech capex jumped +37.4% and software spending +9.6%. Core PCE at 0.32% m/m; 16% trimmed mean at 0.27% m/m and 2.74% y/y, running 75-100bp above pre-COVID pace. Nominal spending growth at ~6% is too strong for inflation to return to target without a productivity surge. Piper Sandler and JPM expect the Fed to hike in December and March. Trade was a 3.3pp drag largely from AI hardware imports (nearly 100% of US high-tech equipment capex is imported).

bullets.title: Value/equal-weight breakout vs. growth; market broadening into defensives and consumer staples
bullets.body: Russell 1000 Value/Growth ratio broke above two-year resistance. XLP outperformed S&P by +304bp in the final week, cumulative +11.7% over the prior month. Sector momentum rankings show Tech +11%, Financials +6%, Energy +4% leading; Consumer Discretionary -11%, Utilities -5%, Consumer Staples -5% lagging. Hedge funds flipped to buying biotech and medtech. Jefferies noted the SPX equal-weight index approaching a four-year breakout. Cash Return factor was the single best performing factor YTD on a long-short basis per 22V Research.

bullets.title: WTI crude +15.2% in October to above $100; oil fourth consecutive monthly gain on Iran tensions
bullets.body: WTI crude rose +15.2% in October to above $100, its fourth straight monthly gain, driven by US-Iran escalation risk. Gulf of Oman crude/product flows fell to 12.5Mb/d from a 17.2Mb/d early-October peak—a 27% decline. Brent hit $116, with Hedgeye targeting $119-122 cycle highs. Oil strength reinforces the inflation-at-short-end-of-yield-curve thesis. 22V Research flagged oil as the top conviction long and gold as 'expensive relative to oil at 38x ratio vs 20x long-term average.' Energy sector was October's top performer at +14%.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Democrats favored; prediction markets show 91% House odds, 67% Senate
bullets.body: Prediction markets assign 91% probability to Democrats winning the House and 67% for the Senate, with 66% for a Democratic sweep overall. Voter engagement hit a record 56% (up 7 points from 2022) with Democrats holding a 10-point enthusiasm advantage. Post-midterm seasonal patterns are universally bullish: S&P 500 positive all 19/19 times since 1950 (+15% avg), Nasdaq positive all 13 times since 1974 (+25% avg). Key sector implications include AI regulation risk under a Democratic Congress and data center buildout subject to election outcomes, particularly the Texas race (~35% of announced AI factory buildouts).

bullets.title: Global central banks universally hawkish: ECB likely hiking December/March, BoJ December likely
bullets.body: ECB held rates but Lagarde confirmed the direction is 'clearly toward further hikes,' with December now 'very likely' and March probable. JPM raised the Euro area headline inflation forecast to 4.0% with energy driving divergence (Italy +5.6%, France +3.8%). BoJ held at 1.25% with Ueda describing a December hike as 'quite likely.' BoC hiked 25bp to 2.50% (first since 2023). BoE expected to hike 25bp to 4.0% next week. Sweden's Riksbank expected to hike 25bp to 2.0%. The global rate cycle remains decisively tightening with no major DM central bank in dovish mode.

bullets.title: Treasury 10-year yield pulled back from 5.36% to ~4.92%; JPM targets 4.75-4.80% on further equity stress
bullets.body: The 10-year yield retraced from a 5.36% peak to ~4.92% as AI/growth concerns temporarily outweighed inflation worries. JPM technical strategy sees further extension to 4.75-4.80% if equity selling intensifies. The 30-year broke bearish TREND thresholds per Hedgeye. 2s/10s curve steepened, with JPM recommending 2-year forward 5s10s steepeners. JPM Fixed Income continues to look for a December Fed hike and recommends 10s/30s steepeners. HG bond spreads stabilized as tail risks faded, while HY spreads trade 10-18bp inside YTD wides.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex sustainability debate intensifies; 2027 consensus implies massive ramp from current run rates
bullets.body: Consensus 2027 capex implies +16% at AMZN, +59% at META from Q3'26 run rates. MSFT capped quarterly spend near $50-60B. 22V Research flagged that hyperscaler Q3 capex came below expectations, requiring an 'incredible ramp' in 2027 to hit consensus. Shareholder pressure on AMZN and GOOGL around negative FCF and AI ROI may intensify. The 2026 hyper-capex forecast was revised up only 1%—the lowest revision in 3+ years—flagged as a late-cycle signal by Evercore. Jefferies data shows this was the 3rd largest notional sell week for Tech in five years, with AI trade lagging massively.

bullets.title: Anthropic S-1 reveals DeepSeek/Chinese model competitive risk to US frontier models
bullets.body: 22V Research highlighted that DeepSeek and Chinese open-weight models win decisively on 'cost-per-finished-task' for routine work, with distillation from US frontier labs enabling low-cost Chinese outputs. US frontier models retain advantages on complex tasks. Anthropic's S-1 showed compute revenue per dollar improving 5.2x from Q1'25 to Q2'26, but the company needs ~$200B+ ARR by 2027 exit to cover compute commitments. Open-source models have the most room to take enterprise share; closed-source trusted platforms will dominate consumer. DeepSeek's capital raise and Moonshot expansion are flagged as 2027 signposts.

bullets.title: Data center power shortfall of 49GW by 2028E; utilities raising capex plans to capture AI demand
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's global data center capacity model projects 316GW by 2030E at 23% CAGR, with a 49GW US utility power shortfall by 2028E. GE Vernova orders surged +96% organically with guidance raised; Vertiv organic orders grew +100%+. AEP expanded its 5-year capex plan to $100B through 2031 and guides 9-11% operating EPS CAGR. Loudoun County's proposed data center approval pause and Virginia power delivery constraints represent emerging local opposition risk that is beginning to shift voter preferences toward Democrats in proximity to facilities.

bullets.title: $6.3B Binance hack largest crypto exchange breach on record; Bitcoin fell to $76.7K
bullets.body: Binance suffered a $6.3B security breach from a compromised device, with ~$3B frozen on-chain via Tether, Circle, and Ripple. Bitcoin fell 4.6% to $76.7K following the breach. Morgan Stanley expects downside risk to COIN/GEMI 2027 earnings and valuation multiples. HOOD fell -13.5% on earnings miss and the crypto overhang. Crypto miners BTBT, RIOT, and MARA fell 9-12%. Morgan Stanley views this as a custody and operational failure, not a blockchain flaw, and sees greater potential for custody-execution separation rather than wholesale migration to DEXs.
